To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the piston-cylinder friction power loss increases with an increase in the piston speed, stroke length, and the piston-cylinder clearance.
the friction power loss is a function of piston speed, piston-cylinder clearance, piston-cylinder geometry and the oil viscosity.
the minimum oil film thickness is directly proportional to the cylinder bore diameter and inversely proportional to the piston speed.

the following aspects: • Modeling of the piston–cylinders interaction using Reynolds equation • Finite Difference solution of Reynolds equation • Parametric study to infer the impact on piston–cylinder friction loss.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the frictional loss is significantly affected by the piston-cylinder clearance, piston speed and piston stroke length.
the piston–cylinders friction power loss can be significantly reduced by increasing the stroke length and decreasing the bore diameter of the cylinder.

the piston-cylinder friction loss can be minimized by reducing the piston speed, reducing the cylinder diameter, increasing the piston diameter, increasing the oil viscosity, increasing the oil supply pressure and increasing the oil volume.
